findings.checklist_item: Enumerate the probe's four REST calls (endpoint + verb) and require the verdict to rest on an independent READ-BACK of the Epic Link field, not on the PUT's status code, since DC returns 204 while ignoring the write.
evidence: Plan: 'four predetermined REST calls' — none are named.
Plan (related-gap section): 'set_parent's non-sub-task branch has no read-back verification ... If the Epic Link clear silently no-ops, that is invisible today.'

1a9f pattern already proven on this instance: DC answers a parent write with HTTP 204 and silently ignores it (_hierarchy.py set_parent read-back rationale), so status code alone cannot settle the verdict.
findings.finding: The plan describes the probe as 'four predetermined REST calls' but never enumerates them, their endpoints/verbs, or — critically — how the probe READS BACK to distinguish a real clear from an accepted-and-ignored no-op. This is load-bearing because set_parent's non-sub-task branch has no read-back today (the plan itself flags this), so a bare HTTP 204 does not prove the clear.
findings.location: Section 'THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN' (the probe design) and the AC1 verdict
scenarios: Probe PUTs {epic_link: null}, gets 204, and reports 'CLEARS' without re-reading — the same 204-but-ignored trap 1a9f documented, yielding a false-positive verdict that the re-home is then built on.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: (1) GET issue to confirm the Epic Link is set; (2) PUT {epic_link_field_id: null}; (3) GET issue again and assert the field is now empty; (4) optionally the search-backed get_parent_map read — and record all four raw request/response bodies as the AC1 evidence.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a probe run that errors or cannot reach DC is handled (distinct from a definitive does-not-clear verdict) so it is not mistaken for a product defect.
evidence: Probe makes 'four predetermined REST calls' against live DC 8.17.1
AC1 requires 'its verdict ... is recorded here' but verdict is binary (CLEARS / does NOT clear)
An unreachable/errored DC yields neither verdict
findings.finding: The probe has three possible outcomes (CLEARS, does-not-clear, and probe-errored/DC-unreachable), but the acceptance criteria only branch on the first two; an errored probe run produces no recordable verdict and stalls the ticket without a defined disposition.
findings.location: THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN + AC 'the probe runs in CI and its verdict on {epic_link: null} is recorded here'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note that the probe distinguishes CLEARS / DOES-NOT-CLEAR / INCONCLUSIVE, and that only a definitive DOES-NOT-CLEAR triggers the product-defect branch; INCONCLUSIVE re-runs.

findings.checklist_item: State the probe's auth/HTTPS/harness preconditions (boot the digest-pinned DC harness, wait on /rest/api/2/serverInfo, set JIRA_DC_BASE_URL, mint an admin PAT the way conftest.py's jira_dc_pat / the capability-map job do) so the CI probe in AC1 is actually runnable.
evidence: Plan: 'A targeted, deterministic probe is added by this ticket: scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py + .github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml ... four predetermined REST calls' — no auth/base-URL/readiness preconditions stated.

.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml handles all of this: 'Wait for Jira DC to become ready' on /rest/api/2/serverInfo, JIRA_DC_BASE_URL: http://localhost:2990/jira, and jira_dc_capability_map.py '(mirroring tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py's jira_dc_pat fixture) — Mints its own admin Personal Access Token via POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens'.
AC1 requires 'the probe runs in CI and its verdict ... is recorded here' but the plan does not say how the probe authenticates to or reaches the harness.
findings.finding: The plan adds a NEW CI probe workflow (.github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml) and script, but states no auth/base-URL/harness-readiness preconditions for it — unlike the capability-map workflow it contrasts against, which boots the digest-pinned harness, waits on /rest/api/2/serverInfo, sets JIRA_DC_BASE_URL, and mints an admin PAT via POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens.
findings.location: Section 'THE BLOCKING UNKNOWN' / new artifacts scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py + .github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml
scenarios: The probe workflow is authored without booting the harness / minting a PAT and cannot reach DC, or 401s, and the verdict on AC1 is never obtained.
The probe silently talks to the wrong base URL and returns a false 'clears' verdict.
findings.suggested_fix: Have jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml reuse the capability-map job's harness boot + readiness wait + JIRA_DC_BASE_URL, and have the probe script mint its PAT via POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens mirroring tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the DC-harness boot (build + serverInfo poll + teardown) should be factored into a reusable `workflow_call` step reused by the smoke lane, the capability map, and this new probe — or record why a third standalone copy is acceptable here.
evidence: search_files '.github/workflows' for 'docker compose up -d --build' returns exactly two existing hits: external-integration.yml:521 and jira-dc-capability-map.yml:77 — both wrapped in the same 240x /rest/api/2/serverInfo poll + logs-on-failure + `docker compose down -v` on always

Repo pattern: _artifact-probe.yml, _build-and-test.yml, _optionality.yml are reusable `on: workflow_call` bodies invoked by multiple lanes specifically so lanes 'cannot drift' — but the DC harness boot has NO reusable form
This is config/near-duplication, not justified complexity: the shared recipe already exists twice and the plan adds a third copy rather than reusing one
findings.finding: The new probe workflow would add a THIRD verbatim copy of the Jira DC harness boot recipe (docker compose up --build; poll /rest/api/2/serverInfo; logs-on-failure; teardown-on-always) already duplicated across external-integration.yml's jira-dc-harness job and jira-dc-capability-map.yml, in a repo that otherwise factors shared job bodies into reusable workflow_call files.
scenarios: A future change to the harness boot (image re-pin, readiness-timeout bump, teardown flag) must be edited in three places or silently drift between the smoke lane, the capability map, and this probe
